Data advertised by dark web sellers reportedly included the names of Hong Kong Metropolitan University (HKMU) students, Hong Kong identity card numbers, telephone numbers, addresses and grade point averages (GPAs). item.dc:creator: Associated Press

item.title: Hundreds attend mass for Tai Po fire victims as bishop dismisses talk of pressure

Both sides were still trying to reach common ground on a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on military-related crisis communication and prevention, sources said on condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to speak on the matter publicly. item.author: Amber Wang
item.dc:creator: Amber Wang
item.description: New state media footage has surfaced showing for the first time what appears to be a Chinese-modified variant of the Russian-origin Kh-29T air-to-surface missile mounted on a J-10C fighter jet. State broadcaster CCTV’s social media account posted a video on Wednesday featuring Chinese fighters, showing the missile mounted under the 4.5-generation fighter as it took off, according to posts by Chinese military bloggers over the weekend. item.author: Peter Wynn Kirby
item.dc:creator: Peter Wynn Kirby
item.description: Many see the US war on Iran as a colossal geopolitical bungle, failing to secure its larger strategic objectives. Yet it has allowed the blundering Trump administration to move into an immensely powerful position – one it seems ready to embrace. With its new-found sway over Venezuela’s oil reserves, degradation of Iranian exports and selective sanctions on Russian oil, Washington has unexpectedly acquired several important levers of the global petroleum trade. Iran has worked hard to play...
item.title: A disastrous Iran war? The US is now a mover and shaker of oil markets

item.author: Danny Mok
item.dc:creator: Danny Mok
item.description: A public housing resident in Hong Kong has lost more than HK$800,000 (US$101,960) worth of cash and gold jewellery that disappeared from her flat in Ngau Tau Kok, prompting a police investigation. Police said the 41-year-old woman filed a report at about 11.55am on Sunday after discovering the items were missing from her home in Kwai Fai House, Lower Ngau Tau Kok Estate. The missing items included gold jewellery worth about HK$500,000 and HK$310,000 in cash, bringing the total loss to about...
item.title: Hong Kong police investigate theft of HK$810,000 in cash, gold jewellery from flat

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced three men to death by hanging over a deadly church shooting, as the kingdom’s Christmas celebrations were cancelled in solidarity with the victims’ families. Gunmen killed nine people and wounded 25 others when they stormed a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Hammoud village, Karak governorate, on October 23. Authorities said three men, two Jordanian brothers and their relative by marriage, had fled after the attack and were arrested three days...
item.title: Jordan sentences 3 men to death over deadly church attack

item.author: Chao Kong
item.dc:creator: Chao Kong
item.description: Science prizes usually put the spotlight on winners, celebrating their discoveries but paying little attention to the researchers left out. A study by scientists at the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) has found that prominent innovation awards may discourage colleagues from pursuing unconventional research – with the most prestigious prizes having the strongest negative effect. The findings raise questions about the wider consequences of scientific honours, including the Nobel Prize, as...
item.title: More Nobel winners, less innovation? Chinese study reveals cost of top-tier awards

item.author: Reuters
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Hamas said on Sunday that a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli air strike, with the Israeli ‌military confirming his death. Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of the Rafah brigade, was killed on Saturday, said the Palestinian militant group’s armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades. The Israeli military said it had killed Abu Younis in a strike in the southern Gaza Strip overnight, ⁠adding that he had led the Rafah brigade...
item.title: Top Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza

item.author: Alyssa Chen
item.dc:creator: Alyssa Chen
item.description: China and Southeast Asian nations have made progress in negotiating a code of conduct for the South China Sea, with Manila announcing that roughly 80 per cent of the draft agreement is complete. Yet whether the long-awaited accord can meet its year-end deadline comes down to Beijing and regional claimants finding common ground on key concessions, according to a Chinese expert. Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said on Saturday after a series of Asean ministerial meetings that 77 per...
item.title: South China Sea code of conduct: can Beijing and Asean meet 2026 deadline?

item.author: Alice Yan
item.dc:creator: Alice Yan
item.description: A tombstone for a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) doctor, engraved with 100 prescriptions she developed, has gone viral on mainland social media, with many people praising her generosity and noble character. The tombstone is in Xiping county, in central China’s Henan province. It commemorates Yuan Shufang, who practised TCM for eight decades and died in 2006 at the age of 97. It recently attracted widespread attention online after local news outlet Dahe News reported on it in early...
item.title: China TCM doctor defies medical secrecy by carving 100 private prescriptions on her tombstone

item.author: Victoria Bela
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bela
item.description: Genetic diversity is nature’s insurance policy – an evolutionary safety net that provides the building blocks for natural selection. While members of the same species share a mostly identical genome, a sliver of unique genetic variants determines their individual traits. When this diversity erodes, and a population becomes more uniform, it could leave them vulnerable to the same threats and unable to adapt when new ones emerge. In China, scientists have found that common songbird species were...
item.title: Evolutionary threat: Chinese mountain birds lost nearly half genetic diversity in 50 years

item.author: Lam Ka-sing
item.dc:creator: Lam Ka-sing
item.description: Hongkongers will experience the chilliest days of autumn this coming week, with temperatures expected to drop to 16 degrees Celsius (61 Fahrenheit) as a cold front sweeps across the southern Chinese coast. The expected drop to 16 degrees on Friday and Saturday may mark the coldest days of the month, falling below the previous low of 17.5 degrees recorded in the city on November 10, according to records on the Hong Kong Observatory’s website. Temperatures earlier in the month remained above 17.5...
item.title: Hongkongers face chilliest days of the season as cold front brings wind and rain

item.dc:creator: Holly Chik
item.description: Chinese ambassador to the United States Xie Feng has signalled high hopes for major-power cooperation at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen this week, while promoting a China-led AI alliance for regional prosperity. The prosperity theme was also highlighted in Qiushi, the Communist Party’s flagship publication, which compiled a series of President Xi Jinping’s previous Apec speeches on building an “Asia-Pacific community with a shared future”. item.author: Edith Lin
item.dc:creator: Edith Lin
item.description: Hong Kong’s police chief has dismissed concerns that geopolitical tensions could affect attendance at the coming Interpol general assembly to be held in the city, saying transnational cooperation on policing is “inevitable”. item.title: Geopolitics won’t affect Interpol assembly in Hong Kong: police chief

item.author: Theodora Yu
item.dc:creator: Theodora Yu
item.description: The charred body of an elderly woman was found in a flat in Hong Kong’s Wong Tai Sin after a blaze broke out on Sunday morning, with officers uncovering a large amount of clutter piled up to the ceiling. The Fire Services Department received a report at 8.45am of a blaze at a lower-floor flat in Lung Kwong House at Lower Wong Tai Sin Estate. Firefighters arrived a few minutes later and put out the blaze at 9.16am. Some 300 people were evacuated, while a female resident on an upper floor was...

item.author: Liu Zhen
item.dc:creator: Liu Zhen
item.description: China has upgraded its VT-4 series main battle tank with cutting-edge technologies aimed at the international market, newly surfaced photos show ahead of the country’s premier defence exhibition in Zhuhai. The appearance of the new tank, believed to be designated as VT-4B, indicates significant upgrades over the existing VT-4A in its armour protection, active protection, weapon station and electronic equipment. item.title: China’s upgraded VT-4B export tank gets fourth-gen Type 100 tech ahead of Zhuhai show

item.author: Ralph Jennings
item.dc:creator: Ralph Jennings
item.description: Chinese and South Korean shipping through the Arctic Ocean to Europe has increased this year, although unpredictable ice, high costs and lapses in demand have exposed the challenges of navigating the route, an environmental research group has found. During the late summer and early autumn shipping season, delays forced one Chinese operator to extend some journeys from 20 days to 30 days, the Oslo-based Bellona Foundation said in a report. Traffic along the Arctic seaway has been busier than last...
item.title: Sudden ice, high costs: are China’s Arctic shipping ambitions at risk after traffic surge?

item.dc:creator: The Korea Times
item.description: The South Korean government said Nvidia’s existing partnership commitments to Seoul remain intact despite disgraced CEO Jensen Huang’s departure from the artificial intelligence giant. However, uncertainties linger as remarks by Elon Musk and others suggest that much of the cooperation may have relied on Huang’s personal verbal commitments. item.dc:creator: Cheryl Arcibal
item.description: The United Arab Emirates, a favoured destination for foreign property investment, could see support for housing demand and prices if heavy midterm losses for US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party help bring an end to the Iran war, analysts said, adding that housing markets across the wider Middle East could also benefit. Police said on Sunday that the incident happened at 1.39am, when the victims – a 65-year-old man and a 58-year-old woman – were crossing the road near Hay Wah Building in Wan Chai while the taxi was travelling west along Hennessy Road. With the 11.30am cut-off time fast approaching, the fourth batch of leisure swimmers, which had 700 spaces allocated to it, were left on dry land when organisers pulled the plug at 9.25am, some 20 minutes after the waves of the race’s slowest entrants...

item.dc:creator: Caroline Lin
item.description: China’s bricks-and-mortar bookstores are increasingly counting on coffee, merchandise and cultural events rather than books to stay afloat – a survival strategy whose tensions were laid bare after a major chain asked a book buyer to vacate its cafe seating unless she bought a drink. item.author: Tribune News Service
item.dc:creator: Tribune News Service
item.description: When Iran’s military planners prepared to hit American bases in the Middle East, they relied on intelligence from an unlikely source: US service members themselves. According to security experts and even the US military, Iran harvested data from social media accounts, fitness apps and even ads to establish patterns of life in US bases across the region. item.author: Theodora Yu
item.dc:creator: Theodora Yu
item.description: Hong Kong must proactively expand trade networks and not “wait for luck to come our way”, as artificial intelligence development that has driven recent growth in exports may gradually slow down, the city’s commerce chief has said. Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau Ying-wah said on Sunday that Hong Kong’s September export growth rate – the highest monthly figure in more than 40 years – was driven by an increase in re-export volume equivalent to 1.4 times the city’s...
item.title: Hong Kong must expand trade networks as AI development could slow, commerce chief says

item.author: Vincent Tan
item.dc:creator: Vincent Tan
item.description: Malaysia’s plans to allow registered refugees to work legally have raised hopes among their communities that have long relied on precarious informal employment to survive, even as Thailand’s experience suggests that such a move is only part of the solution. Thailand has reportedly thousands of refugees taking up formal jobs under a scheme introduced last year. As for Malaysia’s initiative, refugee advocates say it will need clear registration procedures and workplace safeguards to make it...

item.author: Xinyi Wu
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Wu
item.description: China has ushered artificial intelligence into its cinemas, but the country’s first fully AI-generated feature film has flopped at the box office. Made with no human actors or camera crew, Sanxingdui: Future Past brought in just around 1.8 million yuan (US$270,000) after three weeks in theatres, according to Chinese box office data tracker Beacon Pro. item.author: Edith Lin,Lam Ka-sing
item.dc:creator: Edith Lin,Lam Ka-sing
item.description: Internationally acclaimed pianist Yuja Wang has denied making a last-minute change to a recent performance in Hong Kong that led to full refunds to concertgoers, saying the organiser was told weeks in advance about the revision and that she refused to be a “scapegoat” over the controversy. item.dc:creator: Lexi Tian
item.description: Hong Kong International Airport has become the world’s first to deploy robots to repaint runway markings, cutting the time needed to refresh centre lines by about 67 per cent compared with manual painting, its managing authority has said. item.description: Alina Radulescu, 38, has stayed in Italy, the United States and Thailand for months at a time. Now, the IT consultant from Romania shares a co-living space in Seoul with 11 other digital nomads – and says she’s never been happier. “There’s a certain vibe in Korea,” she said. “These days, I’m just so happy when I realise that I’m living here.” Her affinity for South Korea grew gradually through friends in Romania and dance classes where her teacher played K-pop. The test taker, who ranked first in both rounds of the national qualification exam held in April and July, submitted a written confession through his lawyer and acknowledged using AI to obtain answers during the tests. Depicted as emissaries from an advanced civilisation, the bald, blue-skinned digital figures have humanlike bodies and glowing markings across their heads.
